title: Cone-apex equivalence respects coherent cocone composition
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent transformations and Kan mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], ordered join cones of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and sharp join coslices of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison]. Let $K$ be any small simplicial set, $q:C\to D$ any functor of quasicategories in a fixed containing universe, and $c:K^{\triangleright}\to C$ any diagram. Put $f=c|_K$, $x=c(*)$, and let $\gamma:f\to\Delta_Kx$ be the coherent cocone induced by $c$. For a diagram $d:T\to C$ and a vertex $W$ of $C$, put $U_d^C(W)=C_{d/}\times_C\{W\}$, the strict apex fiber of the sharp join coslice; define $U_{qd}^D(qW)$ similarly. These fibers are Kan complexes. For each $W$, the strictly commuting restriction square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}U_c^C(W)&\longrightarrow&U_f^C(W)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
U_{qc}^D(qW)&\longrightarrow&U_{qf}^D(qW)\end{array}$$
is equivalent, as a coherently commuting square of spaces, to
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\operatorname{Map}_C(x,W)&\xrightarrow{\alpha\mapsto\Delta_K(\alpha)\gamma}&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,C)}(f,\Delta_KW)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\operatorname{Map}_D(qx,qW)&\xrightarrow{\beta\mapsto\Delta_K(\beta)(q\gamma)}&\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(qf,\Delta_K(qW)).\end{array}$$
Here an equivalence of squares retains the displayed composition homotopies, not merely the maps on homotopy classes, and induces a weak equivalence between their path-space pullback comparison maps. The corner equivalences are induced by the sharp-to-coherent cocone comparison and restriction of cocones on $K^{\triangleright}$ to its apex. The comparison is natural in $q$, in $W$ with coherent postcomposition, and under restriction $L\to K$ with its induced cone map. No colimit or fibration hypothesis is imposed; $K=\varnothing$ is included.

proof.text: Put $S=K^{\triangleright}$, and for $d:T\to C$ write $M_d(W)=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(T,C)}(d,\Delta_TW)$ and $R_d(W)=\{d\}\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(T,C)}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\operatorname{Fun}(T,C))\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(T,C)}\{\Delta_TW\}$, with the two endpoint evaluations understood. The functor-cone calculus makes the functor categories quasicategories and $M_d(W)$ Kan. Apply the join-slice comparison to $d=c,f$ and also to $qc,qf$. It makes the four sharp apex fibers Kan and gives equivalences $U_d^C(W)\to R_d(W)$. The pinch comparison gives natural homotopy equivalences $M_d(W)\to R_d(W)$. All restriction and $q$ maps commute with this zigzag, since both comparisons are precomposition with their specified collapse maps. Thus it suffices to identify the restriction square on the four $M$ spaces, retaining its commutation data.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.1.5 and Corollaries 4.2.1.7-4.2.1.8; Kerodon 01L5; application to the four diagrams, with the agent notation M and R.

proof.text: Apply the cone-monomorphism lemma to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$. Its cone map is exactly $i:\{*\}=\varnothing^{\triangleright}\hookrightarrow S$, so $i$ is right anodyne even when $K$ is not a quasicategory. The coherent-cocone assertion of the anodyne-cocones lemma, with $A=\{*\}$, $B=S$, $p=c$ and $T=W$, therefore makes actual apex evaluation $E_C:M_c(W)\to\operatorname{Map}_C(x,W)$ a weak equivalence. Here $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,C)=C$ by the internal-functor definition. The same argument gives $E_D:M_{qc}(qW)\to\operatorname{Map}_D(qx,qW)$. Evaluation commutes strictly with $q$ on the specified pinched mapping spaces. Neither application assumes a fibration or a colimit.

source.place: Lemma 4.3.7.8, with A empty; Proposition 7.2.1.3 (02N3) and the opposite dual of Proposition 7.2.2.1 (02NR), (1) implies (6).

proof.text: Construct a simplicial map $s:S\times\Delta^1\to S$ as follows. In an $n$-simplex $\sigma$ of the ordered join, let $a$ be the length of its initial $K$-block ($0\leq a\leq n+1$). For $t:[n]\to[1]$ let $b$ be the length of the initial zero-block. Retain the initial $\min(a,b)$ vertices of the $K$-simplex and put all remaining vertices at the apex; an empty retained block means the pure apex simplex. For a monotone operator, the retained block is the inverse image of the intersection of these two initial blocks, which is also the intersection of their inverse images. This proves compatibility with all simplicial operators, including empty blocks. Thus $s(-,0)=\mathrm{id}_S$, $s(-,1)=*$ and $s(*,t)=*$. Consequently $\eta=c\circ s:c\to\Delta_Sx$ is a coherent transformation whose apex component is $1_x$. On $K\times\Delta^1$ the formula is precisely the ordered-block collapse defining the coherent cocone $\gamma$ of $c$. This construction commutes with every induced cone map $L^{\triangleright}\to K^{\triangleright}$.

source.place: Definition 3.1.1.2 supplies the cone context; agent explicit degreewise ordered-block contraction, not a theorem asserted by HA.

proof.text:
We identify the composition homotopy explicitly in the unpinched model $R_c(W)$. An $n$-simplex is a map $\tau:S\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to C$ with endpoints $c$ and the constant $W$. Form the rectangle
$$F_\tau(z,v,t,u)=\tau(s(z,t),v,u).$$
Its bottom edge ($u=0$) is $\eta$, its top edge ($u=1$) is $1_{\Delta_SW}$, its left edge ($t=0$) is $\tau$, and its right edge ($t=1$) is $\Delta_S(\tau_*)$. Split the $(t,u)$ square along the diagonal from $(0,0)$ to $(1,1)$. The lower-right triangle witnesses that this diagonal is a composite of $\eta$ and $\Delta_S(\tau_*)$; the upper-left triangle witnesses that it is a composite of $\tau$ and $1_{\Delta_SW}$. These statements hold with the entire $\Delta^n$ parameter and commute with all operators on it. Apply the fixed-vertex triangle-space equivalence and unit homotopy in the mapping-composition node to these two triangles, and then the natural pinch equivalence. They give a homotopy of maps of spaces between $\tau\mapsto\tau$ and $\tau\mapsto\Delta_S(\tau_*)\eta$. This uses the Kan spaces of triangles and their restriction maps as spans of equivalences, so it requires no functorial choice of horn fillers.

source.place: Corollaries 4.6.8.5 and 4.6.8.8, Construction 4.6.8.9 and Proposition 4.6.8.11; agent application to the displayed parametrized rectangle.

proof.text:
Restrict both triangles of the preceding rectangle along $K\hookrightarrow S$. The left edge becomes restriction $r_C(\tau)$, the bottom becomes $\gamma$, and the right becomes $\Delta_K(E_C\tau)$. Thus the retained homotopy is
$$r_C\simeq g_CE_C,\qquad g_C(\alpha)=\Delta_K(\alpha)\gamma.$$
Perform the same construction in $D$ to obtain $r_D\simeq g_DE_D$ with $g_D(\beta)=\Delta_K(\beta)(q\gamma)$. The composition maps and their homotopies are those of the coherent Hom bifunctors, rather than just their actions on components. Applying $q$ to $F_\tau$ gives exactly $F_{q\tau}$, and applying $q$ to either of its two triangles gives the corresponding triangle for $q\tau$. The naturality of the induced Hom transformation therefore supplies the compatibility between these horizontal homotopies and the vertical maps. In particular the resulting cube compares the original constant commutation homotopy of $r_C,r_D$ to the displayed composition commutation homotopy of $g_C,g_D$, with its boundary paths homotopic relative endpoints.

source.place: Corollary 8.3.5.8 and Remark 8.3.5.9 (03PD), applied to the two triangles; the rectangle and its restriction are the agent proof of the required homotopy.

proof.text: For $W\to W'$, the second-variable action of the coherent Hom bifunctor postcomposes the rectangles, and its composition and unit homotopies identify $\Delta_K(a)(\Delta_K(\alpha)\gamma)$ with $\Delta_K(a\alpha)\gamma$. The same coherent bifunctor supplies all higher compatibilities, including those with $q$. For $j:L\to K$, step 3 gives $s_K(j^{\triangleright}(z),t)=j^{\triangleright}(s_L(z,t))$ degreewise. Hence the entire rectangle and its two triangles restrict to the construction for $cj^{\triangleright}$, and $\eta|_L$ is the restricted cocone. Apex evaluation commutes with these restrictions. Combined with the natural sharp-to-coherent and pinch comparisons of step 1, these identities establish all three claimed naturalities for the square of spaces.

source.place: Coherent Hom functoriality, together with HTT 4.2.1.5-4.2.1.8 for naturality of the corner zigzags; agent substitution into the rectangle.

proof.text: Use the four corner equivalences of step 1, followed at the two left corners by $E_C,E_D$ from step 2, and use the two horizontal homotopies with their cube coherence from step 5. These form a zigzag of coherent comparisons of squares whose corner maps are weak equivalences. Apply the coherent-cube invariance lemma, whose comparison uses precisely these specified side homotopies. It gives an isomorphism of the path-pullback targets in the homotopy category of Kan complexes, represented by a weak-equivalence zigzag, and identifies the two comparison maps up to the retained homotopy. Together with the weak equivalence of their sources, this is the asserted weak equivalence between comparison maps. It does not substitute an arbitrary commutation homotopy for the one obtained from cocone composition.

source.place: Context only: Proposition 7.1.6.9; the actual path-pullback conclusion uses the cited agent coherent-cube lemma, whose statement explicitly retains side homotopies.

proof.text: If $K=\varnothing$, then $S=\Delta^0$, $E_C,E_D$ are identities, and $M_f(W)$ and $M_{qf}(qW)$ are the one-point mapping spaces in $\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,C)=\Delta^0$. Thus both squares are the same map-to-point square. In general some cocone spaces may be empty; none of the constructions selects a cocone or a vertex in such a space, so all arguments apply unchanged. The existence of the stated diagram $c$ already supplies $x$, and $W$ is fixed as in the assertion.
